newsitem.title: USA: Applied Magnetics offers $1.76 billion for Read-Rite.
newsitem.headline: Applied Magnetics offers $1.76 billion for Read-Rite.

text.p: Computer disk drive maker Applied Magnetics Corp. said Monday it offered to acquire disk drive component maker Read-Rite Corp. for $1.76 billion in stock.
Under the proposed terms of the deal, Read-Rite shareholders would receive 0.679 common shares of Applied Magnetics for each Read-Rite share.
Based on the closing price of Applied Magnetics on Feb 21, the exchange ratio would produce a value of $37.50 for each Read-Rite share, said Applied Magnetic.
Read-Rite closed Monday up $3.81 at $32 on Nasdaq. Applied Magnetic stock dropped $2.375 at $52.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Applied Magnetics, based in Goleta, Ga., also said it would seek to replace Milpitas, Calif.-based Read-Rite's current board of directors with a new board that would, subject to their financial duties, endorse the transaction.
The combination of the two companies, said Applied Magnetics, would result in a supplier of disk heads with $1.8 billion sales per year, and an equity market capitalisation of of $3.4 billion.

Applied Magnetics, a maker of disk drives, also said that cost savings, manufacturing efficiencies and revenue enhancements from the combination would provide incremental gains in pretax earnings of more than $100 million in the 12 months following the transaction.
The total value of the deal, according to an Applied Magnetic spokesman, is $1.76 billion. Read-Rite has about 47 million shares outstanding.
Speaking of the merger, the Applied Magnetics spokesman said, "Our intention is to have it friendly." But he added that "We have been trying to do this for nine months and they have said no."
Representatives from Read-Rite were not immediately available for comment. Read-Rite makes recording heads, head assemblies for computer disk drives.
